decisive_items: Intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos were identified
Patient had history of kidney transplant in 2004 causing immunocompromised status.
Two distinct, well-defined, umbilicated skin-colored lesions
response.rationale: Intracellular yeast forms with surrounding halos in an immunocompromised transplant patient strongly support cutaneous cryptococcosis, with the umbilicated nodules also characteristic. Histoplasmosis is the closest alternative but is less directly supported by the halos/capsular morphology.

rejected.why: Painless nodules may occur in sporotrichosis, but histopathology shows encapsulated yeast, not sporotrichotic yeast forms or a sporotrichoid pattern.
Arborizing telangiectasias and ulceration mimic basal cell carcinoma, but the yeast-containing histiocytic infiltrate excludes carcinoma.
Ulcerated nodules can resemble cutaneous leishmaniasis, but intracellular yeast with halos is not consistent with Leishmania amastigotes.
Ulceration and crusting can mimic squamous cell carcinoma, but there is no squamous proliferation and the histopathologic yeast is definitive.
